entries.ff87baf88b1dc952c16f6cabf815440f2b4f30a3: <reference osisRef="1Sam.30.30-1Sam.30.31">1Sa 30:30-31</reference> <hi type="italic">Hormah</hi> in the Negeb (<reference osisRef="Josh.15.30">Jos 15:30</reference>) is <hi type="italic">Zephath</hi>, the present <hi type="italic">Zepáta</hi>, on the western slope of the <hi type="italic">Rakhma</hi> plateau (see at <reference osisRef="Josh.12.14">Jos 12:14</reference>). <hi type="italic">Cor-ashan</hi>, probably the same place as <hi type="italic">Ashan</hi> in the <hi type="italic">shephelah</hi>, upon the border of the Negeb, has not yet been discovered (see at <reference osisRef="Josh.15.42">Jos 15:42</reference>). <hi type="italic">Athach</hi> is only mentioned here, and quite unknown. According to Thenius, it is probably a mistaken spelling for <hi type="italic">Ether</hi> in the tribe of Simeon (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.7">Jos 19:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.15.43">Jos 15:43</reference>). <hi type="italic">Hebron</hi>, the present <hi type="italic">el Khulil</hi>, Abraham’s city (see at <reference osisRef="Josh.10.3">Jos 10:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.23.17">Gen 23:17</reference>).  <chapter eID="1Sam.30"/> <div eID="gen4194" type="x-p"/>

                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XXX.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p>AND it came to pass, when David and his men were come to Ziklag on the third day <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">To wit, after <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s departure from <ns0:hi>Achish;</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>Zik<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lag</ns0:hi> was at a great distance from the Camp and place of Fight, as appears from 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 1. 2. and <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s men being all Foot-men, could make but slow Marches.</ns0:note>, that the Amalekites <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">The re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mainders of that People who lived near those parts where <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> had destroyed their Brethren, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 27. 8, 9.</ns0:note> had invaded the south <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">To wit, the Southern part of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> and the adjacent parts: See below, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14.</ns0:note>, and Ziklag, and smitten Ziklag <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Sacked and spoiled it.</ns0:note>, and burnt it with fire:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 And had taken the women captives that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> therein: they slew not any <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Which was strange, considering how <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> dealt with them, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 27. 9. But this must be ascribed partly to their selfish or fleshly Interest: for they might reserve them, ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther to make Sale of them for their Profit, or to abuse them for their Lust; or, it may be, to revenge themselves upon <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> and his men, by reserving them to extraordinary, and lingring, and repeated punishments; but principally, to Gods over-ruling and wonderful Providence, who set these bounds to their Rage; and though he designed to chastise <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s sin and folly, yet would not deliver him nor his up to death.</ns0:note>, either great or small, but carried <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> away, and went on theIr way.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 ¶ So David and his men came to the city, and behold, <ns0:hi>it was</ns0:hi> burnt with fire, and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters were taken captives.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 Then David and the people that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> with him, lift up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Till either the humour was wholly spent, or the consi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deration of their Calamity had made them stupid.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And Davids two wives were taken captives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal, the Carmelite.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And David was greatly distressed: for the people spake of stoning him <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">As the Author of their miseries, by coming to <ns0:hi>Ziklag</ns0:hi> at first, by provoking the <ns0:hi>Amalekites</ns0:hi> to this cruelty, by his forwardness in Marching away with <ns0:hi>Achish,</ns0:hi> and leaving their Wives and Children unguarded.</ns0:note>, because the soul of all the people was <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> bitter.</ns0:note> grieved, every man for his sons, and for his daughters: but David encouraged himself in the LORD his God <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> In this that the All-wise, and All-powerful Lord, was his God by Co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venant-relation, and special Promise, and true and Fatherly affection, as he had shewed himself to be in the whole course of his Providence towards him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 And David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />melechs son, I pray thee bring me hither the e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phod <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">And put it upon thy self, that thou maist enquire of God according to his Ordinance, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 27. 21. See above, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 23. 9. <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> was sensible of his former Error in neg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lecting to ask counsel of God by the Ephod, when he came to <ns0:hi>Achish,</ns0:hi> and when he went out with <ns0:hi>Achish</ns0:hi> to the Battel; and his necessity now brings him to his Duty, and his Duty meets with Success.</ns0:note>: and Abiathar brought thither the ephod to David.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And David enquired at the LORD, saying, Shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? And he answered him, Pursue, for thou shalt surely overtake <ns0:hi>them,</ns0:hi> and without fail recover <ns0:hi>all</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Before, God answered more slowly and gradually, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 23. 11, 12. but now he answers speedily, and fully at once, because the business here required more haste. So Gracious is our God, that he considers even the degree of our necessi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ties, and accommodates himself to them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 So David went, he and the six hundred men that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left behind, stayed.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 But David pursued, he and four hundred men <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">A small number for such an attempt: but <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> was strong in Faith, giving God the glory of his Power and Faithfulness.</ns0:note>: (for two hundred abode behind, which were so faint, that they could not go over the brook Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sor <ns0:hi rend="sup">o</ns0:hi>).</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And David said unto him, To whom <ns0:hi>belong<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />est</ns0:hi> thou? and whence <ns0:hi>art</ns0:hi> thou? And he said, I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> a young man of Egypt <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">God by his Providence so ordering it, that he was not one of that Cursed Race of the <ns0:hi>Amalekites,</ns0:hi> who were to be utterly destroyed, but an <ns0:hi>Egyptian,</ns0:hi> who might be spared.</ns0:note>, servant to an Ama<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lekite, and my master left me <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">In this place and condition: which was barbarous inhu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manity: for he ought, and easily might have carried him away with the Prey which they had taken. But he paid dear for this cruelty, for this was the occasion of the ruin of him and of all their company<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> And God by his secret Provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence ordered the matter thus for that very end. So that there is no Fighting against God, who can make the smallest accidents serviceable to the production of the greatest ef<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fects.</ns0:note>, because three days agone I fell sick.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 We made an invasion upon the south of the Cherethites <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Philistines,</ns0:hi> as is manifest from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 16. who are so called <ns0:hi>Zeph.</ns0:hi> 2. 5.</ns0:note>, and upon <ns0:hi>the coast</ns0:hi> which <ns0:hi>belongeth</ns0:hi> to Judah, and upon the south of Caleb <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">This is added by way of re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />jection: <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> that part of the South of <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> which be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />longs to <ns0:hi>Caleb</ns0:hi>'s Posterity, <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 14. 13.</ns0:note>, and we burnt Ziklag with fire.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 And David said to him, Canst thou bring me down to this company? And he said, Swear unto me by God, that thou wilt neither kill me, nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring thee down to this company <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">For his Master had told him whither they intended to go, that he might come after them, as soon as he could.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 ¶ And when he had brought him down, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hold, <ns0:hi>they were</ns0:hi> spread abroad upon all the earth <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Secure and careless, because they were now come al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />most to the Borders of their own Countrey, and the <ns0:hi>Phili<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stines</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> both were otherwise engaged, and <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> as they believed with them. So they had no visible cause of danger; and yet then they were nearest so their destru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ction.</ns0:note>, eating, and drinking, and dancing, because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:p n="20">20 And David took all the flocks, and the herds <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">To wit, which the <ns0:hi>Amalekites</ns0:hi> had taken from the <ns0:hi>Philistines</ns0:hi> or others.</ns0:note>

                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The Soldiers, who lately were so incensed against <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> that they spake of Stoning him: now upon this suc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cess Magnifie him, and Triumphantly celebrate his Praise; and say concerning this spoil, <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> purchased <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> by his Va<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lour and Conduct, and he may dispose of it as he pleas<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 ¶ And David came to the two hundred men, which were so faint that they could not follow Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid, whom they had made also to abide at the brook Besor: and they went forth to meet David, and to meet the people that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> with him <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">To congratulate the Victory; which, it is probable, <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> had sent a Messenger to acquaint them with.</ns0:note>; and when David came near to the people, he <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">

                  <ns0:p n="23">23 Then said David, Ye shall not do so, my bre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thren <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">He useth his Power and Authority to over-rule them; but manageth it with all sweetness, calling them Brethren; not onely as of the same Nation and Religion with him, but as his fellow-Soldiers.</ns0:note>, with that which the LORD hath given us <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">What he hath freely imparted to us, we should not unkindly and injuriously with-hold from our Brethren.</ns0:note>, who hath preserved us, and delivered the compa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny that came against us, into our hand.</ns0:p>
